items.title: cloudflare/security-audit-skill
items.summary: Developed by Cloudflare, security-audit-skill is a coding-agent skill designed for multi-stage security audits. It aims to standardize security audits in software development processes by providing machine-readable and independently verified findings.

snapshot.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail
items.summary: DietrichGebert/ponytail is a JavaScript project that directs AI agents to act like the laziest senior software engineer by minimizing the code-writing process. Adopting the principle that the best code is the code that is not written, it aims to address efficiency in development processes with a different approach.

snapshot.description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.

items.title: supabase/supabase
items.summary: Supabase is a development platform that offers a dedicated Postgres database for building web, mobile, and artificial intelligence applications. Written in the TypeScript language, this project aims to simplify database management and application development processes.

snapshot.description: The Postgres development platform. Supabase gives you a dedicated Postgres database to build your web, mobile, and AI applications.

items.title: twentyhq/twenty
items.summary: Twenty offers an open-source alternative to the customer relationship management software Salesforce. This platform is being developed with a focus on artificial intelligence integration.

snapshot.description: The open alternative to Salesforce, designed for AI.

items.title: strelov1/freehire
items.summary: Developed with the Go language, freehire is an open-source (source code accessible and open for development by anyone) search engine designed for job seekers. It provides a platform that allows users to scan and find job postings.

snapshot.description: freehire — the open-source search engine for job seekers

items.title: PHP 8.2.35
items.summary: PHP 8.2.35 is a new security update released for PHP, a server-side scripting language. This version has been made available to users as part of ongoing efforts to improve the overall security of the software.

snapshot.description: Related ongoing thread: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening security - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50182987

items.title: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening security
items.summary: The PHP Foundation announced the security update that comes with PHP 8.2.35 and shared its new strategies for improving the overall security of the software. This work aims to address security vulnerabilities and strengthen defense mechanisms for PHP, a server-side scripting language.

snapshot.description: Related ongoing thread: PHP 8.2.35 - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50180873(links to more at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50184935)

items.title: Meta ordered to pay $25B penalty in New Mexico Cambridge Analytica case
items.summary: The state of New Mexico has ordered the social media company Meta to pay a $25 billion fine as part of the Cambridge Analytica lawsuit. The decision emerged as a result of the legal process regarding the company's practices concerning user data privacy and security.

items.title: There isn't an easy exploit for this PHP vulnerability
items.summary: It is stated that a security vulnerability in PHP does not have a structure that is easily exploitable, contrary to popular belief. By examining the technical details of the vulnerability in question, it is explained why it is difficult for attackers to exploit this flaw.

items.title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
items.summary: LiteLLM version 1.107.0 was replaced on the Python Package Index (PyPI) with malicious code containing a backdoor that steals credentials. LiteLLM, a library used by software developers to integrate language models, put user data at risk with this security breach.

items.title: OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT
items.summary: OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Image-SFT is an artificial intelligence model with text-to-image generation capabilities. Shared on the Hugging Face platform, this model was developed to convert text-based prompts into visual outputs.

items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
items.summary: SpatialScout is a benchmark tool that measures the ability of vision-language models to map 3D scenes and exhibit object-level spatial intelligence through active exploration. Containing eighty different indoor scenes, this study aims to evaluate whether models can create a consistent world representation during autonomous exploration processes.

snapshot.description: Spatial intelligence requires agents to actively acquire visual evidence and integrate observations into a coherent representation of the three-dimensional world. Yet spatial question answering offers limited evidence of whether models can construct accurate metric maps through autonomous exploration. items.title: From VLM Planners to Robotic Agents: Self-Evolving Harnesses for History-Dependent Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language-action models offer successful results by combining visual understanding and action generation processes in robotic manipulation tasks. This article proposes self-improving systems to manage dependencies based on past interactions and reduce execution errors in long-term tasks.

snapshot.description: Vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance across embodied manipulation tasks by unifying visual understanding, language conditioning, and action generation. However, long-horizon tasks can involve non-Markovian dependencies: successful decisions may require retaining task progress and past interaction outcomes, while partial observability and execution errors compound over time. items.title: CompactSplat: Spatially Adaptive Gaussian Distribution for Feedforward Scene Reconstruction
items.summary: CompactSplat is a method that reconstructs 3D scenes from sparse images and uses a spatially adaptive Gaussian distribution instead of distributing equally to every pixel. This approach aims to increase geometric accuracy and texture details without the need for scene-based optimization.

snapshot.description: Reconstructing 3D scenes from sparse views without per-scene optimization remains highly challenging, especially for recovering accurate geometry and fine textures. While recent feedforward approaches leverage generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for scene generation, they typically assign one or multiple Gaussians to each pixel. items.title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
items.summary: The article published on Hugging Face argues that security auditing for graphical user interface (GUI) agents should focus not only on the screenshot but also on the expected transition process following the performed action. It aims to detect security vulnerabilities in interface interactions by integrating the outputs of existing world models into verification processes from formats such as text or code.

snapshot.description: A login screen that appears after a tap on Sign in is expected; the same screen after a tap on View order is an attack. For GUI agents, safety is therefore a property of the transition rather than of the screen, and a monitor that inspects only screens can be defeated by reusing a legitimate one. items.title: PACE: Periodic and Channel-Aligned Encoding of Four-Bit Recurrent States
items.summary: PACE, shared on Hugging Face, is a method that encodes recurrent states used in linear-attention-based language models with four-bit precision. This technique reduces memory usage during inference, allowing more sequences to be processed simultaneously.

snapshot.description: Linear-attention language models keep their context in a recurrent state of fixed size, where an inference system stores one copy of this state for every sequence it decodes at the same time. Storing the state at lower precision therefore lets more sequences share an accelerator. Artificial intelligence models trained on massive data that can understand human language and generate text.
It is a specialized skill or plugin that artificial intelligence agents use to perform a specific task.
It is a method used to take control of or cause a software or system to malfunction by exploiting its security vulnerability.
